body:
This looks to be a bug in eclipse-jdt. There's no explicit formatter setting for `instanceof` pattern matching, it's just the formatter not understanding this syntax. Eclipse version 2021.12, using eclipse-jdt 4.22 works as intended. We unfortunately have to wait for a) the IntelliJ plugin to update the bundled Eclipse libraries and b) Spotless to update eclipse-jdt to 4.22.

I was able to get the IDE to work as intended by configuring the IntelliJ Eclipse Formatter plugin to point to an Eclipse 2021.12 installation, so that at least confirms that version of eclipse-jdt works as intended. That said, we need both IDE and CLI to match otherwise folks will reformat in IntelliJ and spotless with complain or vice versa.

We can open a PR for spotless for this but the [IntelliJ plugin](https://github.com/krasa/EclipseCodeFormatter) doesn't seem to use any kind of dependency management. I suspect the author has to download the updated libraries locally and rebuild.
We aren't the only ones asking for this: https://github.com/diffplug/spotless/issues/1059

> An aesthetic thing for sure but I think it's better with the space than without.

This definitely triggers me as well.

issue.title: Improve performance for role mapping with DNs

labels.name: auto-merge-without-approval
labels.description: Automatically merge pull request when CI checks pass (NB doesn't wait for reviews!)

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
DNs in a role mapping are parsed each time a matching is performed against a user group. If there are large number of role mappings and large number of user groups, this process can be quite slow since DN parsing is non-trivial.

This PR improves the performance by introducing a cache for DN parsing so that an unique DN from all role mappings is only parsed once per user (regardless of how many groups the user has). The cache stores the normalized string format of the DN instead of the DN object itself since DN is rather memory expensive. The cache's lifecycle is tied to the UserData model which goes out of scope once role mapping process is completed. Hence it is short-lived and does not need to externally managed.

Thanks to @tvernum for the original idea.

Co-authored-by: Tim Vernum <tim.vernum@elastic.co>

issue.body: Today these tests know far too much about the inner workings of the class under test. This commit reworks them to execute the action from the outside, and interact with it only via the capturing transport. To verify that responses are released on cancellation we use the `ReachabilityChecker` to check reachability directly, rather than interacting with the `NodeResponseTracker` therein.
